observationsNotFindings: The cross-family propagation of an identity finding is the interesting thing here and it is done carefully. CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 was raised against a different row's join, where artifact and version genuinely disagreed. Applying it here could easily have produced a false narrative that sdk v3 was broken the same way; instead predecessorV3's role states v3's identity correctly as artifact v3 with version 3 and names the real v3 defect, the stale predecessorV1 sentence. The same finding is cited by three other joins, so this is a systematic sweep rather than a one-off.

The defect this version actually repairs is one I have charged in this family of artifacts before: a predecessor role sentence carried forward until it described the wrong version. Live v3's predecessorV1 role read 'This v2 does not reuse the v1 version number' inside a file that was v3. The repair replaces the self-referential formulation with 'Not this artifact's version number', which cannot go stale on the next increment. That is the better fix - it removes the class of defect rather than the instance.

Measurement is genuinely untouched. All nine obligations are object-identical to v3 and the top-level key set is unchanged; the twelve changed leaves are identity, the two descriptive fields, three role sentences, two added pins, one added finding entry, two added recordedInputs and the remeasurement clause. A reader can therefore rely on the v3 measurement review, if one existed, without re-deriving it - though v3 was never independently reviewed, which the artifact states.

OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED remains open and is the obligation with the least movement available to it: reservedVerbatim routes five of its six reserved items to other rows entirely - DR-105, DR-108, DR-007, DR-114 and DR-102 - so only the exact SDK APIs and frameworks limb is DR-125's own to close. That shape is worth the coordinator noting when sequencing DR-125 work.
